title: mlflow agent setup warehouse picker: parse Databricks warehouse JSON field-by-field and list RUNNING warehouses first
answers: Why does the mlflow agent setup SQL warehouse menu show stopped warehouses above running ones?
The warehouse picker in the setup wizard is missing some of my Databricks SQL warehouses when the API response is compact or on one line
Where is the SQL warehouse list built and sorted for mlflow agent setup?
How do I change the order or parsing of warehouses offered by the agent setup wizard?
body:
Path: mlflow/agent/setup/setup.sh:select_warehouse calls mlflow/agent/setup/setup.sh:json_warehouse_rows to turn the Databricks SQL warehouses list response (the JSON from the warehouses API used by the setup wizard's warehouse selection menu) into id|name|state rows for the menu.
Rule: json_warehouse_rows must read each id, name and state key independently of line layout: it first splits each key onto its own line with sed, then emits a row only once id, name and state are all captured (emit_if_complete after every field), so pretty, compact and reordered-field JSON all work. It buckets rows by state, printing RUNNING warehouses first and the rest after, and keeps the API order inside each bucket.
Symptom: With compact one-line JSON, the earlier per-line awk parser kept only the last warehouse on that line, so some warehouses were missing from the menu. Stopped warehouses could also appear above running ones.
Constraints: Applies to the Databricks warehouse selection in the agent setup script only; the menu still ends with the 'Enter a warehouse ID' option. Do not reintroduce per-line awk rules that assume one key per line or a fixed field order. Covered by tests/agent/test_setup_sh_unit.py:test_json_warehouse_rows_lists_running_warehouses_first (pretty, compact and reordered-field cases).
applies: Shell parsing of Databricks SQL warehouse lists in mlflow agent setup (setup.sh); not the Python warehouse API client.
says: The SQL warehouse picker in the setup wizard is missing several of our available warehouses.
Stopped warehouses appear above running ones in the setup wizard selection menu.
Display active, running SQL endpoints at the top of the warehouse list during setup.
The warehouse dropdown omits compute resources when the provider returns compact single-line data.
Make the warehouse selection prompt reliably show all clusters regardless of server response format.
search: In mlflow/agent/setup/setup.sh, json_warehouse_rows parses Databricks SQL warehouse list JSON field-by-field and sorts RUNNING warehouses before stopped ones. To support compact, pretty, and reordered JSON without omitting warehouses, keys are split per line using sed and emitted once id, name, and state are captured. Rows are bucketed by state while preserving API order within each bucket, and the selection menu retains the final option to manually enter a warehouse ID. This applies only to Databricks warehouse shell parsing in setup.sh and is verified by test_json_warehouse_rows_lists_running_warehouses_first in tests/agent/test_setup_sh_unit.py.
